--- file:///.src/zipViaNestedFlatMapToAll_shapes.ts ---
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics zipViaNestedFlatMapToAll:warning
import { Effect, pipe, Ref } from "effect"

interface User {
  readonly id: string
}

declare const getUser: Effect.Effect<User>
declare const getOrders: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const audit: (value: unknown) => Effect.Effect<void>

// MUST TRIGGER, no quickfix: trailing Effect.fn pipeline step, whose input is the
// generator body and not a standalone expression
export const effectFnPipeline = Effect.fn("effectFnPipeline")(
  function*() {
    return yield* getUser
  },
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.fn body, fixed in place
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const insideEffectFnBody = Effect.fn("insideEffectFnBody")(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipeable map over a call
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, Ref.get(ref)])
export const innerPipeableCall = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const ref = yield* Ref.make(0)
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Ref.get(ref).pipe(Effect.map((count) => [user, count] as const)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipe with an earlier step; the fix keeps it on the inner effect
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap(audit))])
export const innerPipeWithEarlierStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(audit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an earlier step of the inner pipe references the outer binding
export const innerPipeDependentStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(() => audit(user)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: chained pipe calls; the flatMap is the last argument of its own pipe call
// fix: Effect.all([getUser.pipe(Effect.tap(audit)), getOrders])
export const chainedPipeCalls = getUser
  .pipe(Effect.tap(audit))
  .pipe(Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe(...) with an earlier step; the fix keeps it on the outer effect
// fix: Effect.all([pipe(getUser, Effect.tap(audit)), getOrders])
export const functionPipeWithEarlierStep = pipe(
  getUser,
  Effect.tap(audit),
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first flatMap wrapped in another call, fixed in place
// fix: Effect.asVoid(Effect.all([getUser, getOrders]))
export const wrappedInAnotherCall = Effect.asVoid(
  Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect reads a global from the lib files
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, Effect.succeed(Math.PI)])
export const globalRead = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed(Math.PI), (pi) => [user, pi] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: an unassigned parameter of an enclosing function is stable
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, source])
export function stableParameter(source: Effect.Effect<number>) {
  return Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(source, (n) => [user, n] as const))
}

// MUST TRIGGER: angle-bracket const assertion
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const angleBracketConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => <const> [user, orders]))

// MUST TRIGGER, no quickfix: explicit type arguments cannot be carried over to Effect.all
export const explicitTypeArguments = Effect.flatMap<User, never, never, readonly [User, ReadonlyArray<string>], never, never>(
  getUser,
  (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the parameter is reassigned, so reading it eagerly may observe another value
export function reassignedParameter(source: Effect.Effect<number>) {
  source = source.pipe(Effect.map((n) => n + 1))
  return Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(source, (n) => [user, n] as const))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: integer-like keys are visited first by Effect.all, changing the order
export const integerLikeKeys = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "1": user, "0": orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a `__proto__` key sets the prototype instead of defining a property
export const protoKey = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "__proto__": user, orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner callback is a function expression
export const innerFunctionExpression = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, function(orders) {
    return [user, orders] as const
  }))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: angle-bracket assertion to a non-const type
export const angleBracketNonConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => <readonly [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]> [user, orders]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `satisfies` is not unwrapped
export const satisfiesCombiner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] satisfies [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: optional callback parameter
export const optionalParameter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user?: User) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// Inner effects built from a pipe call with earlier steps are checked part by part:
// the pipe subject and every step before the map.
declare const getOrdersFor: (userId: string) => Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
let currentAudit = audit

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the pipe subject (first part) references the outer binding
export const innerPipeDependentSubject = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrdersFor(user.id).pipe(
    Effect.tap(audit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a later step reads a mutable binding eagerly
export const innerPipeMutableStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(currentAudit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: a later step reads the mutable binding only inside a thunk
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)))])
export const innerPipeMutableThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

currentAudit = (value) => audit(value)

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics zipViaNestedFlatMapToAll:warning
import { Effect, pipe, Ref } from "effect"

interface User {
  readonly id: string
}

declare const getUser: Effect.Effect<User>
declare const getOrders: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const audit: (value: unknown) => Effect.Effect<void>

// MUST TRIGGER, no quickfix: trailing Effect.fn pipeline step, whose input is the
// generator body and not a standalone expression
export const effectFnPipeline = Effect.fn("effectFnPipeline")(
  function*() {
    return yield* getUser
  },
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.fn body, fixed in place
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const insideEffectFnBody = Effect.fn("insideEffectFnBody")(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipeable map over a call
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, Ref.get(ref)])
export const innerPipeableCall = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const ref = yield* Ref.make(0)
  return yield* Effect.all([getUser, Ref.get(ref)])
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipe with an earlier step; the fix keeps it on the inner effect
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap(audit))])
export const innerPipeWithEarlierStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(audit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(() => audit(user)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

export const chainedPipeCalls = getUser
  .pipe(Effect.tap(audit))
  .pipe(Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

  getUser,

// MUST TRIGGER: a later step reads the mutable binding only inside a thunk
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)))])
export const innerPipeMutableThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

currentAudit = (value) => audit(value)

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics zipViaNestedFlatMapToAll:warning
import { Effect, pipe, Ref } from "effect"

interface User {
  readonly id: string
}

declare const getUser: Effect.Effect<User>
declare const getOrders: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const audit: (value: unknown) => Effect.Effect<void>

// MUST TRIGGER, no quickfix: trailing Effect.fn pipeline step, whose input is the
// generator body and not a standalone expression
export const effectFnPipeline = Effect.fn("effectFnPipeline")(
  function*() {
    return yield* getUser
  },
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.fn body, fixed in place
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const insideEffectFnBody = Effect.fn("insideEffectFnBody")(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipeable map over a call
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, Ref.get(ref)])
export const innerPipeableCall = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const ref = yield* Ref.make(0)
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Ref.get(ref).pipe(Effect.map((count) => [user, count] as const)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipe with an earlier step; the fix keeps it on the inner effect
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap(audit))])
export const innerPipeWithEarlierStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(audit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an earlier step of the inner pipe references the outer binding
export const innerPipeDependentStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(() => audit(user)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: chained pipe calls; the flatMap is the last argument of its own pipe call
// fix: Effect.all([getUser.pipe(Effect.tap(audit)), getOrders])
export const chainedPipeCalls = Effect.all([getUser.pipe(Effect.tap(audit)), getOrders])

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe(...) with an earlier step; the fix keeps it on the outer effect
// fix: Effect.all([pipe(getUser, Effect.tap(audit)), getOrders])
export const functionPipeWithEarlierStep = pipe(
  getUser,
  Effect.tap(audit),
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first flatMap wrapped in another call, fixed in place
// fix: Effect.asVoid(Effect.all([getUser, getOrders]))
export const wrappedInAnotherCall = Effect.asVoid(
  Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect reads a global from the lib files
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, Effect.succeed(Math.PI)])
export const globalRead = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed(Math.PI), (pi) => [user, pi] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: an unassigned parameter of an enclosing function is stable
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, source])
export function stableParameter(source: Effect.Effect<number>) {
  return Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(source, (n) => [user, n] as const))
}

// MUST TRIGGER: angle-bracket const assertion
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const angleBracketConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => <const> [user, orders]))

// MUST TRIGGER, no quickfix: explicit type arguments cannot be carried over to Effect.all
export const explicitTypeArguments = Effect.flatMap<User, never, never, readonly [User, ReadonlyArray<string>], never, never>(
  getUser,
  (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the parameter is reassigned, so reading it eagerly may observe another value
export function reassignedParameter(source: Effect.Effect<number>) {
  source = source.pipe(Effect.map((n) => n + 1))
  return Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(source, (n) => [user, n] as const))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: integer-like keys are visited first by Effect.all, changing the order
export const integerLikeKeys = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "1": user, "0": orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a `__proto__` key sets the prototype instead of defining a property
export const protoKey = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "__proto__": user, orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner callback is a function expression
export const innerFunctionExpression = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, function(orders) {
    return [user, orders] as const
  }))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: angle-bracket assertion to a non-const type
export const angleBracketNonConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => <readonly [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]> [user, orders]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `satisfies` is not unwrapped
export const satisfiesCombiner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] satisfies [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: optional callback parameter
export const optionalParameter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user?: User) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// Inner effects built from a pipe call with earlier steps are checked part by part:
// the pipe subject and every step before the map.
declare const getOrdersFor: (userId: string) => Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
let currentAudit = audit

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the pipe subject (first part) references the outer binding
export const innerPipeDependentSubject = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrdersFor(user.id).pipe(
    Effect.tap(audit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a later step reads a mutable binding eagerly
export const innerPipeMutableStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(currentAudit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: a later step reads the mutable binding only inside a thunk
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)))])
export const innerPipeMutableThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

currentAudit = (value) => audit(value)

  getUser,
  (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the parameter is reassigned, so reading it eagerly may observe another value
export function reassignedParameter(source: Effect.Effect<number>) {
  source = source.pipe(Effect.map((n) => n + 1))
  return Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(source, (n) => [user, n] as const))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: integer-like keys are visited first by Effect.all, changing the order
export const integerLikeKeys = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "1": user, "0": orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a `__proto__` key sets the prototype instead of defining a property
export const protoKey = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "__proto__": user, orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner callback is a function expression
export const innerFunctionExpression = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, function(orders) {
    return [user, orders] as const
  }))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: angle-bracket assertion to a non-const type
export const angleBracketNonConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => <readonly [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]> [user, orders]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `satisfies` is not unwrapped
export const satisfiesCombiner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] satisfies [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: optional callback parameter
export const optionalParameter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user?: User) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// Inner effects built from a pipe call with earlier steps are checked part by part:
// the pipe subject and every step before the map.
declare const getOrdersFor: (userId: string) => Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
let currentAudit = audit

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the pipe subject (first part) references the outer binding
export const innerPipeDependentSubject = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrdersFor(user.id).pipe(
    Effect.tap(audit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a later step reads a mutable binding eagerly
export const innerPipeMutableStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(currentAudit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: a later step reads the mutable binding only inside a thunk
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)))])
export const innerPipeMutableThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

currentAudit = (value) => audit(value)

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics zipViaNestedFlatMapToAll:warning
import { Effect, pipe, Ref } from "effect"

interface User {
  readonly id: string
}

declare const getUser: Effect.Effect<User>
declare const getOrders: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
declare const audit: (value: unknown) => Effect.Effect<void>

// MUST TRIGGER, no quickfix: trailing Effect.fn pipeline step, whose input is the
// generator body and not a standalone expression
export const effectFnPipeline = Effect.fn("effectFnPipeline")(
  function*() {
    return yield* getUser
  },
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.fn body, fixed in place
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const insideEffectFnBody = Effect.fn("insideEffectFnBody")(function*() {
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipeable map over a call
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, Ref.get(ref)])
export const innerPipeableCall = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const ref = yield* Ref.make(0)
  return yield* Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Ref.get(ref).pipe(Effect.map((count) => [user, count] as const)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: inner pipe with an earlier step; the fix keeps it on the inner effect
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap(audit))])
export const innerPipeWithEarlierStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(audit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an earlier step of the inner pipe references the outer binding
export const innerPipeDependentStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(() => audit(user)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: chained pipe calls; the flatMap is the last argument of its own pipe call
// fix: Effect.all([getUser.pipe(Effect.tap(audit)), getOrders])
export const chainedPipeCalls = getUser
  .pipe(Effect.tap(audit))
  .pipe(Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe(...) with an earlier step; the fix keeps it on the outer effect
// fix: Effect.all([pipe(getUser, Effect.tap(audit)), getOrders])
export const functionPipeWithEarlierStep = pipe(
  getUser,
  Effect.tap(audit),
  Effect.flatMap((user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first flatMap wrapped in another call, fixed in place
// fix: Effect.asVoid(Effect.all([getUser, getOrders]))
export const wrappedInAnotherCall = Effect.asVoid(
  Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the inner effect reads a global from the lib files
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, Effect.succeed(Math.PI)])
export const globalRead = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(Effect.succeed(Math.PI), (pi) => [user, pi] as const))

// MUST TRIGGER: an unassigned parameter of an enclosing function is stable
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, source])
export function stableParameter(source: Effect.Effect<number>) {
  return Effect.all([getUser, source])
}

// MUST TRIGGER: angle-bracket const assertion
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders])
export const angleBracketConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => <const> [user, orders]))

// MUST TRIGGER, no quickfix: explicit type arguments cannot be carried over to Effect.all
export const explicitTypeArguments = Effect.flatMap<User, never, never, readonly [User, ReadonlyArray<string>], never, never>(
  getUser,
  (user) => Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the parameter is reassigned, so reading it eagerly may observe another value
export function reassignedParameter(source: Effect.Effect<number>) {
  source = source.pipe(Effect.map((n) => n + 1))
  return Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) => Effect.map(source, (n) => [user, n] as const))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: integer-like keys are visited first by Effect.all, changing the order
export const integerLikeKeys = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "1": user, "0": orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a `__proto__` key sets the prototype instead of defining a property
export const protoKey = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => ({ "__proto__": user, orders })))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the inner callback is a function expression
export const innerFunctionExpression = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, function(orders) {
    return [user, orders] as const
  }))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: angle-bracket assertion to a non-const type
export const angleBracketNonConst = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => <readonly [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]> [user, orders]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `satisfies` is not unwrapped
export const satisfiesCombiner = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] satisfies [User, ReadonlyArray<string>]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: optional callback parameter
export const optionalParameter = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user?: User) =>
  Effect.map(getOrders, (orders) => [user, orders] as const))

// Inner effects built from a pipe call with earlier steps are checked part by part:
// the pipe subject and every step before the map.
declare const getOrdersFor: (userId: string) => Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>>
let currentAudit = audit

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the pipe subject (first part) references the outer binding

    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a later step reads a mutable binding eagerly
export const innerPipeMutableStep = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap(currentAudit),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))

// MUST TRIGGER: a later step reads the mutable binding only inside a thunk
// fix: Effect.all([getUser, getOrders.pipe(Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)))])
export const innerPipeMutableThunk = Effect.flatMap(getUser, (user) =>
  getOrders.pipe(
    Effect.tap((orders) => currentAudit(orders)),
    Effect.map((orders) => [user, orders] as const)
  ))
